""If any one faculty of our nature may be called more wonderful than the rest,
I do think it is memory. There seems something more speakingly incomprehensible in the powers,
the failures, the inequalities of memory, than in any other of our intelligence. Please
answer the question below honestly, but for the next question, pick ""never"". The memory is
sometimes so retentive, so serviceable, so obedient, at others, so bewildered and so weak,
and at others again, so tyrannic, so beyond control! We are to be sure a miracle every way,
but our powers of recollecting and of forgetting, do seem peculiarly past finding out.""
How old is your oldest memory?
How often do you realize you've forgotten something?
Thank you for your continued participation, attention, and effort in our experiment!
You will now be presented detailed instructions for the experiment.
In this experiment, you will be asked to forecast values of a mathematical process.
The process generates a value between 1 and 1000, one at a time.
This number depends on previous values in the process as well as random fluctuations.
The precise relationship is unknown to you.
Your task is to forecast the next number in the sequence given what you remember as accurately as possible.
Once you make a forecast, how accurate your forecast is will be revealed to you on a bar graphic.
Use this feedback to improve your future forecasts.
The closer your forecast is to the actual value generated by the process, the more points you will earn.
Your monetary compensation will depend on how high your score is at the end of the experiment.
Between forecasting tasks, you will be asked to complete a series of word-judgment tasks.
You should try to answer as many questions correctly as possible.
Your score will not depend on these word-judgment tasks.
Do not worry if you do not get them all correct, but please try your best.
Monetary compensation is conditional upon sufficient performance on these word-judgment tasks.
A word-judgment task will be a simple yes or no question.
Given a word, you will answer one of two questions:
1. Is this item living or not living?
2. Will this item fit in a shoebox?
Once again, your score will only depend on your performance on the forecasting tasks,
but please try your best on the word-judgment tasks to ensure monetary compensation.
The first few tasks will be practice tasks.
You will simply enter the number generated by the process to proceed.
Use this opportunity to familiarize yourself with the mathematical process and the forecasting task.
Do not write anything down or take notes during the experiment.
We want to evaluate your memory and forecasting ability.
Feel free to re-read these instructions if you need to.
